questions.title: Finite-time stochastic bandit regret and empirical validation
questions.description: Develop a complete source-assisted research analysis of UCB1 for independent iid reward streams on [0,1]. Consult Auer, Cesa-Bianchi and Fischer (2002), Finite-time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem, DOI 10.1023/A:1013689704352, Theorem 1 and its proof (author-hosted paper: https://homes.di.unimi.it/cesa-bianchi/Pubblicazioni/ml-02.pdf). Maintain reviewable Markdown/LaTeX definitions, assumptions, equation-level derivations and unresolved claims. Define the observed filtration, nonanticipating choices, arm pull counts, gaps, expected regret and random pseudo-regret. Derive the finite-horizon suboptimal pull-count bound and resulting gap-dependent expected regret bound with the paper's constants, initialization and integer rounding accounted for. Handle adaptive random sample counts rigorously rather than inserting them directly into a fixed-sample tail bound. Explain tied optimal arms, short initialization horizons and what the theorem does not imply about pathwise regret, tight constants or unbounded rewards. Implement the public UCB1 decision interface using model-authored Python, optionally NumPy/SciPy primitives. Related third-party code such as SMPyBandits may be inspected and attributed, but does not replace the requested implementation or constitute original-author replication. Use exploratory code and simulation to challenge the mathematical claims and implementation, then obtain independent review of the exact current theory and code. Freeze a confirmatory experiment using at least two distinct Bernoulli bandits (including a tied-optimum case) and one non-Bernoulli bounded-reward bandit, with at least 1000 independent complete bandit trajectories per design and at least two reported horizons, the larger at least 4096. Include a unique-optimum design, state true means and gaps, compare UCB1 to uniform exploration and a purely empirical-greedy baseline, and report pull allocations, mean cumulative pseudo-regret, trajectory-level Monte Carlo standard errors, the published bound and execution failures. In unique-optimum designs, test a prospectively defined meaningful improvement over uniform exploration, not merely the generally loose theoretical upper bound; target regret MCSE divided by expected uniform regret at the largest horizon at most 0.01. Handle the zero-gap case without dividing by zero. Freeze seeds, horizons, precision and criteria before confirmation, do not interpret nested horizons as independent replications, and report all unmet criteria. Bind derivations, generated implementation, actual diagnostics, independent review and confirmation into a final research report with honest limitations. This is a full known-result research task, not blind rediscovery, novelty, original-paper/code reproduction or a required Lean proof.

request_fields.name: counts
request_fields.meaning: Completed pull counts for a batch of independent bandit histories. The number of completed plays in each row is its count sum.
request_fields.shape: B by K nonnegative integers; 1 <= B <= 2048 and 2 <= K <= 10; each row sum <= 10000000.
request_fields.indexing: Zero-based batch and arm indices; rows can have different count sums.
request_fields.edge_cases: All-zero rows and partially initialized rows are valid. No future rewards, known means, horizon or simulator state are supplied.

request_fields.name: reward_sums
request_fields.meaning: Cumulative observed reward for each arm in each history.
request_fields.shape: B by K finite numbers with 0 <= reward_sums[b][i] <= counts[b][i].
request_fields.indexing: Exactly the same batch and arm order as counts.
request_fields.edge_cases: Unpulled arms have reward sum zero. Only valid requests are evaluated; no malformed-input taxonomy is imposed.

response_fields.name: arms
response_fields.meaning: The next selected arm for each row under the UCB1 policy. Until every arm is pulled, select the lowest-index unpulled arm. Subsequently maximize empirical mean plus sqrt(2 * natural_log(completed_plays) / arm_count); break exact maximum ties by lowest arm index.
response_fields.edge_cases: Each row is processed independently. The logarithm uses completed plays, not the next round or an external horizon. The deterministic tie convention fixes the ABI without changing the theorem's regret bound.
response_fields.normalization: Empirical mean equals observed reward sum divided by that arm's count; inputs are already in [0,1] reward units.

invariants.meaning: The returned decision depends only on the supplied observed counts and reward sums. Do not inspect simulator state, future outcomes or true means. Do not call a prebuilt bandit-policy implementation; numerical primitives are allowed.
Do not mutate the request. Identical requests return identical selections. Additional output fields are allowed, but arms is required.

empirical_claims.meaning: Run at least two Bernoulli designs including tied optimal arms and one non-Bernoulli [0,1] design, at least 1000 independent trajectories each and two reported horizons with largest >=4096; freeze criteria, seeds and precision before outcomes.

The confirmatory policy actually calls the accepted implementation on past-only histories, updates only the selected arm, and computes counts and cumulative pseudo-regret from true means and chosen arms. No oracle-policy substitution or future-reward access.

Report uniform and empirical-greedy baselines, pull allocation and pseudo-regret with trajectory-level MCSE. A unique-optimum design must show a meaningful prospectively specified improvement over uniform exploration, not only satisfy the loose upper bound. At the largest horizon, regret MCSE divided by positive expected uniform regret must be <=0.01.

Compare mean regret with the derived finite-time expectation bound, while reporting Monte Carlo uncertainty and failures. Nested horizons are not independent replicates. Simulations do not prove logarithmic growth, pathwise bounds or validity beyond bounded iid rewards; zero gaps contribute zero regret without reciprocal-gap division.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: A decision is finite computation on a finite history; the model chooses its own scientific derivation length, diagnostic actions and revision sequence.
